claim: Retained Claude-only ccusage daily costs rise from $2,823.79 and $2,427.25 on October 1/2 to $5,940.56 on October 3. The supplied executor window comparison reproduces exactly from count-only scanner outputs: IET per 24 h rises 2.121 times, counted call rows 2.419 times, and subagents started 2.824 times, while mean context per call falls from 271,790 to 216,230 tokens. The unfiltered retained session-view export is $12,404.88 and its workflow share is 61.402%; removing 17 rows with pre-10-03 last activity leaves $11,151.92, with coordinator-tree shares 63.296% and 33.787%. These are session-selection views, not spend since 10-03. Net pre-first-call attachment growth excluding UI is about 2.9 KB (0.8K rough tokens), rather than the positive-only 4.3 KB (1.2K) estimate. These are scoped observations, not subscription charges or a quality comparison. Adding the retained advisor-cohort estimate gives 830.270M and 1,777.960M IET per 24 h (2.141 times); all 689 A and 1,209 B advisor iterations in those cohorts used Fable. Fable is $2,092.87, or 35.230% of priced Claude dollars on 10-03. The user subsequently selected an Opus 5.5 advisor.
limitations: API-equivalent prices are not the subscription meter. ccusage leaves claude-sonnet-5-5 unpriced; its dollars therefore do not price every counted Claude model.
ccusage days are local time and Prometheus days are UTC. These scopes and the scanner windows must not be summed or equated.
Prometheus keeps one week; this retained export starts with the UTC day 2026-09-27 and ends with 2026-10-03.
The attr byte shares use unfitted weights, so they show direction only; receipt context shares exclude UI records before normalization.
The hook_success records are UI-only and are not counted as context. Pre-first-call attachment sizes are serialized metadata bytes, not exact model input or tokenization.
NativeStack only, because NativeStack2604's telemetry has no listener. This scope is the coordinator's stated observation boundary, not a new listener check.
10-04 is a partial day. The scanner ends at 14:00Z; no full-day projection is a measured total.
This is a re-derivation of retained native outputs and scanner aggregates, not a new provider/model run, an upstream acceptance test, or a quality/savings A/B.

window_compare.py includes synthetic zero-usage rows in its call counts and uses per-field maximum deduplication. Its subagent calls-per-file statistic spans each selected file, whereas its call and IET windows filter call timestamps.

Window hook text is not retained in the aggregate inputs. Historical hook-text estimates are reported as estimates; current installed carrier and upstream static hook sizes are distinct observations and do not establish historical hook outputs.

The unfiltered session export includes pre-10-03 activity: 17 rows worth $1,252.96 have lastActivity before 2026-10-03T04:00Z. The raw and activity-selected shares have different denominators. Filtering lastActivity does not restrict the dates of every token in a session total; neither view is established as spend since 10-03.

The reproduction artifact extends the supplied analysis with advisor-cohort rows. Original executor output is unchanged. Its private raw output includes source identifiers; only sanitized aggregates are retained here.

Advisor iterations are absent from calls.tsv and retained only as per-file tot values in files.jsonl. Grouping them by file first_ts reproduces the reviewed cohorts, but files can cross window boundaries. Executor-plus-advisor-cohort IET is an estimate with mixed timestamp scopes, not an exact call-window total; advisor iterations have no recorded effort here.

IET applies the same coefficients to every model: input 1, cache read 0.1, five-minute and unclassified cache writes 1.25, one-hour cache writes 2, and output 5, with thinking already in output. There is no model-specific base-price multiplier. Advisor aggregates lack cache-write duration splits and weight all cache writes at 1.25. Thus IET model shares and window ratios are relative-index measures, not dollar shares or actual spend ratios; Fable dollars from ccusage remain separate. Historical Fable usage precedes the new Opus advisor decision.
